correctness.rationale: In the infinite universal cover, paths between trivalent hubs are subdivided links of lengths m, n and d, with local hub signatures {m,m,d} and {n,n,d}. If m!=n the signatures distinguish hub types and all three segment types even when numeric segment lengths coincide; equal rooted covers then correspond to actual finite automorphism orbit classes. If m=n!=d, cycle and bridge segments remain distinguished by unequal length, and equal cycles can be exchanged. If m=n=d the homogeneous trivalent cover with uniform subdivisions identifies each cycle-position with bridge-position, despite their different finite cut-vertex status; stable colors are 1+floor(m/2) versus 1+2floor(m/2) finite automorphism orbits. The color-refinement/universal-cover lemma is published (Krebs–Verbitsky). An independent direct 1-WL graph builder confirmed all 588 cases 3<=m<=n<=9, 1<=d<=12, including equality and collision boundaries; infinity case follows structural cover proof, not finite tests.
